hero.heading: How coordination shows up on the dock.
hero.body: Structured examples of how AGL sources, qualifies, and delivers. Metrics and named accounts stay unpublished until verified — we don't invent manufacturer claims.

intro.heading: Pattern recognition, not vanity numbers.
paragraphs: Each entry below is a structural placeholder for a finished case study: the operating context, the spec problem, the sourcing approach, and the freight plan.
Until owner-approved copy lands, titles and outcomes stay unpublished. No fabricated percentages, volumes, or customer logos.

studies.title: Food packaging line
studies.summary: Dual-source stock pallet program with managed inbound freight for a recurring Midwest packaging schedule.

studies.title: Engineered oversize
studies.summary: Custom footprint and deck rating sourced through more than one qualified shop, freight booked to a single receiving window.

studies.title: Multi-plant program
studies.summary: One brokerage relationship covering staggered plant schedules across regional lanes — mills and carriers coordinated from a single desk.

studies.title: Crate and dunnage
studies.summary: Containment package beyond the pallet: crates and dunnage specified with the load, not as an afterthought.

ctaBand.heading: Have a supply problem worth documenting?
ctaBand.body: If your line needs a dual-source plan or a cleaner freight story, we'll build it quietly — and publish the write-up only when the facts are cleared.
